newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO AIM TO PULL AWAY FROM PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO AIM TO PULL AWAY FROM PSG.

text.p: Monaco will be looking to extend a remarkable home record against Paris St Germain when the two sides meet in a top-of-the-table French first division clash at the Louis II stadium on Sunday.
Since their last promotion to the top flight 20 years ago, Monaco have not lost a league match to PSG in the principality, going down just once at home to the Parisians in a French Cup tie in 1993.
Both sides are looking to bounce back from defeat as they lock horns in what could turn out to be the most important match in the league championship this season.
Monaco can pull seven points clear of their rivals if they win. PSG can close the gap to just one point if they win.
The two sides set their hearts on the league title at the beginning of the season after narrowly missing out in May, when Auxerre came from behind to clinch a championship and French Cup double.
Despite their French Cup slip-up at second division Laval last Friday, the odds look stacked in Monaco's favour with the stronger and more confident squad.
PSG won their weekend French Cup game at third division Besancon, but the 6-1 thrashing by Juventus in the European Super Cup last week still weighs heavily on their shoulders.
The PSG players decided against talking to reporters earlier in the week for fear of having to field awkward questions that might destabilise them.
"The longer we spend time with you, the more we lose our concentration," goalkeeper Bernard Lama told reporters.
"With your kind of questions you lead the players to doubt also... Do you want me to leave for Monaco in a losing frame of mind."

PSG reversed their decision on Thursday but spoke cautiously about the importance of the match, while coach Ricardo refused to give hints about his line-up except to say fellow Brazilian Leonardo was recovering from a debilitating bout of flu.
"I have the team in my head but I don't want to give it to (Monaco coach Jean) Tigana," Ricardo said.

Some of Monaco's players also opted for silence before the match, notably Brazilian striker Anderson who is repeatedly being linked with a future move to PSG, and teenager Thierry Henry, who has been courted by Real Madrid.
Scotland's John Collins, with a number of Glasgow derbies against Rangers under his belt from his Celtic days, has no such worries.
He is anxious for the day of the match to come even if the atmosphere at the Louis II stadium, usually quite staid, will not compare with Rangers' Ibrox or Celtic Park.
"It's a match at the top of the championship, representing the technical quality of French football," the midfielder said.
"It also matters in the light of the UEFA Cup and no doubt we're going to be watched with regard to our (quarter-final) match against Newcastle.
"It's our chance to put Paris seven points behind us and take a big step towards the title.
"But we must be careful," Collins said. "This does not mean Paris cannot come back. They have enough talent to still challenge."
"Rai and Leonardo are two players of exceptional talent who can turn a match round, such is their technical strength, vision and confidence and influence on Paris's game."
Collins predicted a very tight match "which could be decided by a dead ball situation or an individual exploit".
Tigana has also kept his line-up to himself, but is without Belgian defender Philippe Leonard, who has a fractured bone in his foot.
PSG's veteran central defender Alain Roche, just back from injury, felt a twinge in his knee in training and is unlikely to be fit. "I don't want to take any risks," he said.
Probable teams:
Monaco - Fabien Barthez, Patrick Blondeau, Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou, Emmanuel Petit, Sylvain Legwinski, John Collins, Ali Benarbia, Enzo Scifo, Anderson, Thierry Henry.
Paris St Germain - Benard Lama, Jimmy Algerino, Paul Le Guen, Bruno N'Gotty, Didier Domi, Benoit Cauet, Vincent Guerin, Jerome Lerot, Rai, Leonardo, Cyrille Pouget.
